newsitem.title: USA: L.A. transit agency prepares for possible strike.
newsitem.headline: L.A. transit agency prepares for possible strike.

text.p: The Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) reported progress on Monday in contract negotiations with its labor unions, but said it was preparing for a possible strike.
Contracts between the MTA and its three major labor unions representing bus and train operators, mechanics, and clerical staff will expire at midnight on June 30.
"Progress is being made at the bargaining table," MTA Interim Chief Executive Linda Bohlinger said in a statement. "The MTA remains hopeful that a strike can be averted."

Bohlinger said, however, that contingency plans would be in place to provide bus and rail service in the county should a strike be called. The contingency service will be ready as early as July 1, the authority said.
The MTA carries an estimated 1.2 million passengers each weekday in a 1,400-square-mile service area throughout Los Angeles County.
